title: Conference Overview
summary: IEEE SSCI 2027 is proposed as an in-person conference on the Gold Coast, with hybrid participation support if needed.

sections.heading: Conference Title and Format
paragraphs: The conference title is IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (IEEE SSCI 2027). The proposed format is in-person, with a hybrid mode supported if needed. Hybrid support would integrate onsite attendance with Zoom-based online presentations within the session schedule.
The proposed conference dates are 14-17 February 2027.

sections.heading: Host City
paragraphs: Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia is proposed as the host city for IEEE SSCI 2027. The city combines global accessibility, ease of travel, cultural vibrancy, and a strong academic presence.

Gold Coast is home to Griffith University, a globally recognized institution with active research in AI, robotics, and computational intelligence. The local academic ecosystem supports international collaboration and makes the region a strong venue for SSCI 2027.

sections.heading: Why Gold Coast
paragraphs: The Gold Coast is a world-renowned destination offering pristine beaches, rainforests, national parks, theme parks, cultural festivals, wildlife encounters, and a safe, walkable, welcoming environment for international guests.
The proposed venue in Broadbeach is centrally located near hotels, transit stops, restaurants, the beach, and major roadways, creating a convenient setting for international attendees.

sections.heading: General Chair Profiles
paragraphs: Professor Alan Wee-Chung Liew is Head of the School of Information & Communication Technology at Griffith University in Australia. He holds a first-class honours B.Eng. in Electrical & Electronic Engineering from the University of Auckland, New Zealand, and a PhD in Electronic Engineering from the University of Tasmania, Australia. He has published extensively in AI and machine learning, computer vision, ensemble and stream learning, and medical imaging. Professor Liew is a Senior Member of IEEE, Fellow of the Australian Computer Society, and Fellow of the Queensland Academy of Arts and Sciences. He serves on multiple editorial boards, including IEEE Transactions, and regularly chairs, organizes, and reviews major international conferences in computational intelligence.

Professor Chin-Teng Lin is a Distinguished Professor at the University of Technology Sydney and a world-renowned expert in artificial intelligence, brain-computer interfaces, and computational intelligence. He received his BSc from National Chiao Tung University, Taiwan, and his MSc and PhD in Electrical Engineering from Purdue University, USA. He was Editor-in-Chief of IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems from 2011 to 2016, is an IEEE Fellow and IFSA Fellow, and received the IEEE Fuzzy Pioneer Award in 2017. Professor Lin has led large-scale multi-year projects and has significant experience in conference leadership, including roles as Program Co-Chair and International Liaison for major IEEE events.

title: Call for Papers and Abstracts
summary: IEEE SSCI 2027 will invite full papers, short papers, late-breaking work, abstracts, and journal-to-conference submissions.

sections.heading: Submission Scope
paragraphs: Following recent IEEE SSCI practice, the program is expected to call for full papers, short papers, late-breaking papers, abstract-only submissions, and journal-to-conference conversions across the conference symposia.

sections.heading: Review Process
paragraphs: The review process is planned to use a centralized conference management system such as CMT3 or EasyChair. Full papers will follow a rigorous double-blind peer-review process with common review guidelines, standardized evaluation criteria, and coordinated acceptance thresholds across symposia.

sections.heading: Paper Review Coordination
paragraphs: Program Chairs will oversee the review process across all tracks to ensure fairness, quality control, and timely completion of reviews.

Workshops will use a different submission deadline, but their review workflow is planned to be hosted on the same platform and follow the same review criteria. Workshop Chairs will be responsible for setting up the workshop review process within the same system, ensuring consistency in reviewer assignment, evaluation standards, and notification procedures.

sections.heading: Session Formats
bullets: Oral presentations: typically 20 minutes for the talk plus 5 minutes for Q&A.
Poster sessions: full paper posters, short paper posters, and late-breaking work or abstract posters.
Panels and interactive sessions: 60-90 minute moderated discussions with academic, industry, and government speakers.
Tutorials and workshops: half-day or full-day sessions, ideally scheduled before the main conference.
Competitions and challenge tracks: live presentations of results and winner announcements.

sections.heading: Keynotes, Panels, and Industry Participation
paragraphs: The conference plans to host distinguished keynote speakers from academia and industry addressing emerging frontiers in computational intelligence. Industry and academic panels will focus on application domains such as healthcare AI, financial AI, energy and transport sustainability, and trustworthy computational intelligence.

A dedicated technology demo and industry exhibition zone is planned alongside the technical program. Industry panels and poster/demo sessions will invite participation from industry, startups, and applied labs.

paragraphs: A sunset welcome reception is planned for the first evening at a scenic outdoor terrace adjacent to the Gold Coast Convention and Exhibition Centre. Delegates will be able to network in a relaxed setting with local cuisine and drinks.

paragraphs: The conference banquet is planned for The Star Gold Coast, minutes from the conference venue. The evening is expected to include a three-course menu highlighting Australian cuisine, live local entertainment such as a didgeridoo performance or Indigenous dance, an awards ceremony, and networking zones.

sections.heading: Career and Startup Sessions
paragraphs: SSCI 2027 will host a Career and Industry Networking Fair where participating companies, research institutes, and government agencies can recruit students, postdocs, and early-career researchers. The event will provide opportunities for one-on-one discussions, resume exchanges, and introductions to potential employers.

A Startup and Innovation Pitch Session will enable early-stage AI and computational intelligence startups to present technologies and business ideas to industry experts, investors, and academic leaders. These sessions aim to promote talent development, foster collaborations, and highlight cutting-edge innovation within the computational intelligence community.

title: Travel Information
summary: Travel information for Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia.

sections.heading: Airports
bullets: Brisbane Airport (BNE) is approximately 85 km from the Gold Coast, just over an hour by car or shuttle. It is a major international hub with direct connections to Asia, including Tokyo, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Seoul; North America, including Los Angeles and Vancouver; and Europe via one-stop flights through hubs such as Doha, Dubai, and Singapore.
Gold Coast Airport (OOL) is approximately 30 minutes from the proposed venue. It provides regional and selected international connections, particularly to New Zealand and Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: Local Transport
bullets: The region is served by the G:link light rail, buses, shuttles, taxis, and rideshare services.
The Gold Coast Convention and Exhibition Centre is centrally located in Broadbeach and is easily accessible from nearby hotels, transit stops, and major roadways.
The Gold Coast Convention and Exhibition Centre is located next to Broadbeach North tram station.
Frequent airport shuttle services and car hire options make intercity travel straightforward.
Recommended hotels are within walking distance of the venue.

sections.heading: Travel Restrictions and Entry
paragraphs: Australia maintains a transparent and streamlined visa system for international visitors. Most participants can apply for an Electronic Travel Authority or eVisitor visa online. Current entry conditions are traveller-friendly, with no major restrictions for most countries in Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

sections.heading: Conference Rates
paragraphs: Negotiated conference rates are not finalized. Several hotels have expressed interest in providing discounted rates, contingent on a minimum number of bookings.

The organizing team plans to finalize hotel agreements in October 2026, once early attendance becomes clearer following the main paper submission deadline. Confirmed conference rates will be published on the conference website no later than November 2026, giving authors and international participants time to plan travel and accommodation.

sections.heading: Transportation Options
